newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-BENFICA BEAT FARENSE TO CLOSE IN ON PORTO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BENFICA BEAT FARENSE TO CLOSE IN ON PORTO.

text.p: Benfica beat Farense 2-1 at home on Sunday to join Porto at the top of the Portuguese league, despite an heroic performance by the Algarve side's Nigerian goalkeeper Peter Rufai.

Porto and Benfica now share first place with 26 points, but Porto have a home game in hand against Maritimo on Monday. Sporting, who suffered an upset defeat on Saturday against Setubal, are trailing in third place with 22 points.

Rufai's series of spectacular saves thwarted Benfica until just before halftime when they opened the scoring with a penalty after captain Joao Pinto was fouled inside the box by Farense defender Carlos Paixao.
Brazilian midfielder Valdo Filho's shot sailed into the left corner of the net while Rufai dived to the right.
Five minutes into the second half Bulgarian midfielder Ilian Iliev extended Benfica's lead to 2-0.
Farense switched from defensive to attacking tactics and scored in the 70th minute with a 20-metre shot from Brazilian substitute striker Fernando Santos.
Benfica defender Helder Cristovao was sent off five minutes from the end for bringing down Farense's Moroccan defender Hajry Redouane.
Sporting compromised their chances of taking the league title which has eluded them for 14 years when they lost 1-0 away to newly-promoted Setubal on Saturday.
Setubal, in fourth place with 19 points, secured their win in the 63rd minute with a header from Ghanaian striker Kwame Ayew.
